name: Sahar Basin
notes: Locked palette: 59 ramp colours, which is the set all rendered sprites are quantized to in CI. Ramps are ordered light -> dark. Reserved bands MUST NOT appear in unit/building/terrain diffuse art; they are applied at runtime by the VFX and team-color systems only.

limestone.role: primary terrain, masonry, concrete, sun-bleached surfaces
limestone.note: Interpolated to twice the original resolution. Nine warm steps across limestone+dust could not carry lit stone: quantizing a building render banded it and pushed mid-tones into gunmetal and olive. Every original entry is retained, so sprites quantized against the narrower ramp are still on-palette. Endpoints and hues are unchanged -- this is more resolution, not a new art direction.

dust.note: Interpolated to twice the original resolution. Nine warm steps across limestone+dust could not carry lit stone: quantizing a building render banded it and pushed mid-tones into gunmetal and olive. Every original entry is retained, so sprites quantized against the narrower ramp are still on-palette. Endpoints and hues are unchanged -- this is more resolution, not a new art direction.

terracotta.role: fired roof tile, parapet coping, trim bands on masonry
terracotta.note: Added for the building set. The reference architecture bands every parapet and coping in fired red, and the warm ramps could not carry it: limestone and dust are desaturated tans, and the only red-orange in the palette was vfx.ember, which is reserved and must stay contrast-safe against fire. Three steps is enough for a band, its shadow, and its underside -- a tile roof does not need a ramp as deep as a wall.

skin.note: Added for the infantry overhaul. The art brief calls for visible skin, and no existing entry could carry it: the warm ramps are ochre rather than rosy, so a face rendered on dust.2 quantized into terracotta and read as blood spatter. Chosen by searching plausible skin HSV for maximum distance from the existing 42 -- these sit 33 from dust.2, their nearest neighbour, which is the same separation terracotta already lives with, and 41 from each other so a face has light and shadow rather than one flat patch. Two entries, not three: a face is about six pixels at gameplay zoom.

shadow.role: cast shadow, occlusion, interiors, night base

grass.role: intended for procedural terrain -- open sward, hedgerow, pasture. Not curated for sprite art; validate_assets.py does not exclude it, so nothing currently stops it appearing there.
grass.note: Added for the Naharin green basin. Neither existing green could carry open ground: olive is a desaturated grey-green for hulls and tarps, and scrub is two entries whose declared role is sparse vegetation. Five steps of 39-43 RGB distance, coarser than limestone's ~31 because five entries span what nine limestone steps span. The ramp stops at grass.4 (#6E9E33) rather than continuing down, because scrub.0 (#6B8A4A) is 31 away and already owns that band -- extending further produced duplicates, not steps. Vegetation is therefore seven steps across two ramps: grass.0-4 then scrub.0 then scrub.1. grass.2 is the open-ground wash: its luminance (177) sits within 5 of limestone.3 (182), which every unit silhouette was tuned for figure-ground against, so the change is hue and not value.

karst.role: the Sur highland's grey limestone -- ridge walls, outcrops, scree chips, the highland haze. Procedural terrain and decor tint only (GH-322).
karst.note: Added for the highland biome (GH-322). Descending brightness like every ramp: index 0 is the lightest. A warm NEUTRAL grey, which no existing ramp holds: gunmetal jumps from luma 96 (gunmetal.2) to 146 (gunmetal.1) and is blue-cast, and limestone.5/6 are warm brown, so every grey composite between them quantised to an olive or limestone entry -- measured in the GH-322 mock as a green rim on a ridge face. `theme_only` keeps it OUT of the terrain quantiser's shared set: a theme opts in by naming it in TerrainTones.paletteRamps (only highland does). Measured before that flag existed: added to the shared set, karst moved the composed terrain of 11 of the 18 non-highland maps -- Beit Sahwan and Wadi Halam among them -- because some arid and green composites sit nearer a karst grey than the entry they used to snap to. packages/app/src/terrain-defaults.test.ts pins every non-highland map against the commit before this ramp existed.

fen.role: the wetland's living green -- open ground, cover verge, low ground and the willow crown. Procedural terrain and decor tint only (GH-871).
fen.note: Added for the wetland biome (GH-871 P2). Descending brightness like every ramp: index 0 is the lightest. A cool, wet green that no existing ramp holds: grass and scrub are drier and yellower, olive is a dusty grey-green, so a wet meadow snapped to one of them read as a field in August. `theme_only` keeps it OUT of the shared quantiser set: a theme opts in by naming it in TerrainTones.paletteRamps (only the wetland does), so no existing map's composed terrain can move.

mud.role: the wetland's wet earth -- the track, ruts, spoil, marsh floor and trunks. Procedural terrain and decor tint only (GH-871).
mud.note: Added for the wetland biome (GH-871 P2), revision 3: a yellower brown than the first cut, after the mood-board look. Descending brightness like every ramp: index 0 is the lightest. Terracotta is too red and limestone too pale for wet ground, so a rutted track snapped to one of them read as a dry road. `theme_only` keeps it OUT of the shared quantiser set; a theme opts in by naming it in TerrainTones.paletteRamps. Dropping the flag moves the composed terrain of shipped maps that are not wetland (recorded in the GH-871 P2 T2 report), which is why packages/app/src/terrain-defaults.test.ts pins all of them.

overcast.role: the wetland's cold overcast stone and sky -- blocked ground, rock faces, slabs and the haze key. Procedural terrain and decor tint only (GH-871).
overcast.note: Added for the wetland biome (GH-871 P2), revision 3: index 1 is a bluer #9FA9B5 so the haze reads as damp air rather than dust. Descending brightness like every ramp: index 0 is the lightest. A cool grey that sits between karst (warm neutral) and gunmetal (blue-cast, with a luma gap): grey composites under a wet sky snapped to one of those and came out warm or olive. `theme_only` keeps it OUT of the shared quantiser set; a theme opts in by naming it in TerrainTones.paletteRamps.

basalt.role: the wetland's dark volcanic boulder. A tint key only -- never in any theme's paletteRamps (GH-871).
basalt.note: Added for the wetland biome (GH-871 P2). One entry, so the descending-brightness rule is vacuous. TINT KEY ONLY: a boulder's rock tint resolves it through paletteColor, but no theme names it in TerrainTones.paletteRamps, so the terrain quantiser never snaps anything onto it and the composed terrain gains no near-black warm entry.

vfx.role: RUNTIME ONLY. Saturated band reserved so explosions and tracers pop against desaturated terrain. Rejected by CI if found in static art.

team.role: RUNTIME ONLY. Applied via palette remap on masked pixels. Author team-color regions in pure magenta #FF00FF in the source .blend material.
team.variants_note: Colour-vision-deficiency alternates of the four colours above, selected by accessibility.colorVision and applied by theme.css's :root[data-cvd=...] blocks and @lions/data's paletteTeamColors(). Gated by tools/src/cvd.test.ts: every pair stays apart by CIE76 ΔE ≥ 25 under Machado et al. 2009 severity-1.0 simulation of its OWN kind, and hostile_text clears 4.5:1 on --bg (tools/src/bad-text-contrast.test.ts). deuteranopia and protanopia share the Okabe–Ito blue/vermillion/yellow triad (indistinguishable dichromacy classes for this palette's own hues); tritanopia keeps kedem and hostile untouched -- they are already ΔE 117 apart under tritanopia -- and only swaps neutral, since S-cone loss is what confuses the default's yellow against sand/limestone terrain, not the blue-vs-red pair. Every entry here is a duplicate hex of one already counted in `colors` above or a fresh pick; validate_data.mjs's total_colors count walks this map alongside `colors` (see its `reserved.<band>.variants` handling) so the count stays honest.

group.role: RUNTIME ONLY. Control-group badge, indexed by group slot 1-9. Since A4 (GH-186) it colours the badge only: the selection ring is team colour, and a group colour survives on a ring only in the flat billboard fallback (a garrisoned unit, or a full ring batch). Never appears in static art.
group.note: Nine hues separated around the wheel and held light enough that the badge's #14150F numeral stays legible at gameplay zoom. g1 keeps the lime the badge always used, so existing muscle memory survives. Deliberately avoids team.hostile, vfx.fire and team.neutral at close range: those already mean enemy, suppression and neutral on the same unit, and a badge that borrows them reads as state rather than membership.
